prompt: Map a family of unchecked exceptions onto status codes: any AppFault reports its own code(), anything else runtime is 500, and a clean run is 200.
explanation: Giving your own exceptions a shared abstract parent lets one catch block handle the whole family while still reading data from the specific subclass -- here code() is declared once on AppFault and inherited by all three. Catch blocks are tried in source order, so the most specific type must come first: catching RuntimeException before AppFault would compile but would turn every 404 into a 500. Unchecked exceptions are the right choice for programmer- and request-level errors because callers should not have to declare them.
hints: One try block, two catch blocks: catch (AppFault fault) first, then catch (RuntimeException other).
The return for the success case goes inside the try, right after action.run().
fault.code() works for every subclass because code() is declared on the shared AppFault parent; getClass().getSimpleName() gives the specific name for describe.
